newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds trail govts in wake of wage data.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds trail govts in wake of wage data.

text.p: Mortgage-backed seccurities firmed late in the session, but participants said that mortgage securities lagged Treasury securities.

U.S. government securities traded higher on news that the Labor Department's Employment Cost Index rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, up from a 0.6 percent advance in the first quarter but in line with a consensus forecast.
Mortgage-backed activity was subdued this session, participants said. One market player, though, reported seeing lists of conventional adjustable rate mortgages out for bid this session.
Market players agreed that down-in- coupon trades are sure to pick up if the 10-year Treasury note plunges below 6.0 percent. Then, some participants may move out of mortgage into Treasuries.
But, some market observers noted that there may come a time when the beaten up sectors -- that is, the premium coupons -- look cheap and offer buying opportunities.
If mortgages get hit too badley, when the dusts settles there will be buying opportunities, said an observer.

The next economic data sure to be watched closely, said participants, is the July payroll report which will be released Friday. A consensus of economists surveyed by Reuters expects the jobless rate to creep down to 4.9 percent.

Late in the session, Government National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 2/32 at 101 23/32 to offer a bond equivalent yield of 7.254. Federal National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 2/32 at 101 18/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5 percent coupons were unchanged at 101 23/32.
Meanwhile, the Treasury's 10-year note was up 6/32 at 103 25/32 to yield 6.10.
